memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"All these officials of yours will come to me, bowing down before me and saying,
'Go, you and all the people who follow you!' After that I will leave.' Then
Moses, hot with anger, left Pharaoh." - Ex 11:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses predicts that Pharaoh's own officials will bow before him and beg Israel
to leave. The proud court of Egypt will plead with a shepherd from Midian.

Then comes a detail we might easily miss: Moses left Pharaoh "hot with anger."
This is the same man Scripture calls the most humble on earth (Num 12:3). Yet
here he is, burning with anger.

We should be careful here. Not all anger is sin. Moses was not angry that his
plans were frustrated. He was angry at hardened rebellion against God, and angry
at the needless suffering Pharaoh's stubbornness was about to bring on his own
people. Jesus Himself looked around at hard hearts "in anger, deeply distressed"
(Mark 3:5).

The test is what our anger is about and what it does. Anger at injustice that
drives us to pray and act rightly is different from anger at being inconvenienced
that drives us to lash out. Ephesians 4:26 says, "In your anger do not sin."

Notice too that Moses did not stay to argue. He said what God gave him to say,
and he left. Sometimes faithfulness means speaking the truth and then walking
away, leaving the outcome with God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What makes you angry, and what does that reveal about your heart?
2. Is there a conversation where you need to speak truth and then let it go?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, teach me to be angry at the things that grieve You and patient with the
people around me. Help me to speak truth and leave the results with You. Amen.
